candidates.exact_span:
FOR THE DRAFT NATIONAL POLLUTANT DISCHARGE ELIMINATION SYSTEM
(NPDES) PERMIT TO DISCHARGE TO WATERS OF THE UNITED STATES
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this document is a draft rather than a final, enforceable permit affects whether numeric limits read from it are enforceable compliance standards (Purpose A) versus informational or non-operative text, and whether monitoring schedules derived from it reflect actually applicable obligations (Purpose B).

Different interpretations of which permit number governs the facility during Federal FY2025 would change which limit schedules, monitoring requirements, and missing-evidence expectations are linked to reported measurements and no-result records.

Facility identity scopes which discharge points, parameters, and monitoring records are in scope; a different interpretation of the permitted entity could change which measurements and obligations are evaluated under each purpose.

candidates.exact_span:
Proposed reissuance of the current National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES)
permit issued September 30, 2016, with an effective date of November 1, 2016, and an
expiration date of October 31, 2021.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The described permit expired before Federal FY2025 (2024-10-01 through 2025-09-30). Interpreting whether the 2016 permit, a proposed reissuance, or some administrative continuation governs during FY2025 would change which numeric limits apply (A), which monitoring requirements were in effect (B), and how absent results should be classified when permit-term applicability is uncertain (C).

candidates.exact_span: San Juan River – San Juan Basin
candidates.computation_change_reason: Receiving-water designation can determine which water-quality-based effluent limits and receiving-water monitoring conditions attach to discharges; a different basin or stream classification could change applicable numeric limits (A) and seasonally or location-dependent monitoring obligations (B).
